title: Puchwein algorithm for calibration sampling — puchwein
text: Puchwein algorithm select samples data matrix iteratively eliminating similar samples using Mahalanobis distance. starts performing PCA input matrix extracts score matrix truncated \(\), number principal components. score matrix normalized unit variance Euclidean distance sample centre data computed, identical Mahalanobis distance \(H\). Additionally, Mahalanobis distances samples comptuted. algorithm proceeds follows: Choose initial limiting distance \(d_{ini}\) Select sample highest \(H\) distance centre Remove samples within minimum distance \(d_{ini}\) sample selected step 2 Go back step 2 proceed samples/observations left dataset Go back step 1 increase minimum distance multiplying limiting distance loop number possible obtain pre-defined number samples selected method. choose adequate number samples, data frame returned puchwein function (leverage) giving observed theoretical cumulative sum leverages points selected iteration. theoretical cumulative sum leverage computed point leverage (sum leverages divided number observations). loop largest difference observed theoretical sums considered producing optimal selection points (subset best reproduces variability predictor space).

title: Savitzky-Golay smoothing and differentiation — savitzkyGolay
text: Savitzky-Golay algorithm fits local polynomial regression signal. requires evenly spaced data points. Mathematically, operates simply weighted sum given window: \[ x_j\ast = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{h=-k}^{k}{c_hx_{j+h}}\] \(x_j\ast\) new value, \(N\) normalizing coefficient, \(k\) gap size side \(j\) \(c_h\) pre-computed coefficients, depends chosen polynomial order degree. sampling interval specified delta.wav argument used scaling get numerically correct derivatives. convolution function written C++/Rcpp faster computations.

Smoothing differentiation data simplified least squares procedures. Anal. Chem. 36, 1627-1639. Schafer, R. W. (2011). Savitzky-Golay filter? (lecture notes). IEEE Signal processing magazine, 28(4), 111-117. Wentzell, P.D., Brown, C.D., 2000. Signal processing analytical chemistry. Encyclopedia Analytical Chemistry, 9764-9800.
